summary: This resolution elects Ms. Mejia to the House Committee on Homeland Security, ranking her immediately after Mr. Walkinshaw.

scores.thoughts: This resolution is a purely procedural measure electing a Member to the Committee on Homeland Security. It contains no provisions related to budgets, appropriations, or any form of government spending.
The bill text addresses only a committee assignment and has no connection to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No healthcare-related content appears in the resolution; it is limited to House committee membership.
The resolution does not mention firearms, regulations, or rights; it is strictly procedural.
While the Committee on Homeland Security has jurisdiction over immigration matters, this bill merely fills a committee seat and does not alter any immigration policy or enforcement.
The resolution contains no language concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
No defense spending, military policy, or related provisions are present in the bill.
The bill has zero engagement with environmental regulations or climate policy.
This procedural resolution does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net issues.
No education policy, funding, or school choice provisions are included.
The resolution is silent on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related matters.
No criminal justice reforms, sentencing, or policing measures are addressed.
The bill text has no relation to trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
Nothing in the resolution pertains to deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The resolution does not engage with LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign aid provisions or international assistance measures are present.
The bill is a committee election resolution but does not alter voting access, election integrity rules, or electoral processes.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight language appears.
The resolution contains no worker protections, union rights, or labor policy content.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil rights protections.
